description: Design a Model Predictive Control (MPC) system that predicts the next state of a system based on the current state and control inputs. The MPC controller will take the current state (2 bits), the control input (2 bits), and will output the predicted next state (2 bits). The next state is calculated as follows: next_state = current_state + control_input (modulo 4).
code:
module mpc_controller (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [1:0] current_state,
    input [1:0] control_input,
    output reg [1:0] next_state
);

always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
    if (reset) begin
        next_state <= 2'b00; // Reset the state
    end else begin
        next_state <= (current_state + control_input) % 4; // Calculate next state
    end
end

endmodule

description: Design a 1-bit DRAM cell with read and write operations. The DRAM cell should have an input data line (D), a write enable signal (WE), a read enable signal (RE), and an output data line (Q). When WE is high, the value on D should be written to the cell. When RE is high, the value in the cell should be placed on Q. Ensure that the cell maintains its state when neither WE nor RE is active.
code:
module dram_cell (
    input wire D,        // Data input
    input wire WE,      // Write enable
    input wire RE,      // Read enable
    output reg Q        // Data output
);

    reg stored_value;    // Internal storage for the 1-bit cell

    always @(posedge WE or posedge RE) begin
        if (WE) begin
            stored_value <= D;  // Write data to the cell
        end
        if (RE) begin
            Q <= stored_value;   // Read data from the cell
        end
    end

endmodule

description: Design a 4-bit up counter with synchronous reset and enable functionality. The counter should increment its value on every clock cycle when the enable signal is high. If the reset signal is high, the counter should reset to 0 regardless of the enable signal. The counter should roll over after reaching 15 (binary 1111).
code:
module up_counter (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input enable,
    output reg [3:0] count
);
    
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            count <= 4'b0000;
        end else if (enable) begin
            count <= count + 1;
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a sample rate converter that takes an input signal sampled at a frequency of 1 kHz and converts it to an output signal sampled at a frequency of 2 kHz. The converter should use a simple zero-order hold method to hold the last sample for an appropriate number of clock cycles.

Implement a Phase-Locked Loop (PLL) where the output phase is adjusted based on an input reference clock and a feedback clock. The PLL should have a simple mechanism to lock the output phase to the reference phase and can be tested with specific test cases.

Design a temperature-based shutdown system that monitors the temperature input and triggers a shutdown signal if the temperature exceeds a certain threshold. The system should have an enable signal that allows the monitoring to be active or inactive. The shutdown signal should remain active until the temperature falls below a safe level, at which point it can reset.
code:
module temp_shutdown(
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input enable,
    input [7:0] temperature,
    output reg shutdown
);
    parameter THRESHOLD = 8'd75; // Shutdown threshold
    parameter SAFE_TEMP = 8'd70; // Safe temperature for reset

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            shutdown <= 0;
        end else if (enable) begin
            if (temperature > THRESHOLD) begin
                shutdown <= 1; // Trigger shutdown
            end else if (temperature < SAFE_TEMP) begin
                shutdown <= 0; // Reset shutdown
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 32-bit timer that can be started, stopped, and reset. The timer increments every clock cycle when it is running. The timer should also have an output to indicate when it reaches a specific countdown value (e.g., 0). The timer control includes start, stop, and reset signals.

Design a 5-stage pipelined processor that performs addition operations. The processor will have the following stages: Instruction Fetch (IF), Instruction Decode (ID), Execute (EX), Memory Access (MEM), and Write Back (WB). Each stage operates on data coming from the previous stage, and the processor should be able to handle 2 input operands and produce a single output result, implementing basic pipelining techniques.

Design a 2-bit up counter that counts from 00 to 11 (0 to 3 in decimal) and wraps around. The counter increments on each positive edge of the clock and has an active-low reset that resets the counter to 00.

Design a 24-bit digital-to-analog converter (DAC) controller in Verilog. The controller should take a 24-bit input signal and enable a corresponding output signal. The output should be a simple representation of the input value, where the output is driven high when the input value exceeds a certain threshold (for example, 0x800000).

Design an RSA encryption module in Verilog that takes a 16-bit plaintext input, an 8-bit exponent, and a 16-bit modulus. The module should output the encrypted ciphertext. The RSA encryption operation is performed using the formula: ciphertext = (plaintext ^ exponent) mod modulus. Ensure the exponent is a valid positive integer and modulus is greater than the plaintext.
code:
module rsa_encrypt(
    input wire [15:0] plaintext,
    input wire [7:0] exponent,
    input wire [15:0] modulus,
    output reg [15:0] ciphertext,
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            ciphertext <= 16'b0;
        end else begin
            if (modulus > 0 && plaintext < modulus) begin
                ciphertext <= plaintext ** exponent % modulus;
            end else begin
                ciphertext <= 16'b0; // Invalid input case
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description:
Design a Voltage-Controlled Oscillator (VCO) that generates a frequency output based on a control voltage input. The VCO should have the following specifications:

3. The output frequency should be represented as a 16-bit number.
4. The design must include a clock signal to enable frequency updates on each clock cycle.

    output reg [15:0] F_out
);
    parameter Frequency_base = 10_000_000; // 10 MHz
    parameter Multiplier = 1_000_000; // 1 MHz
    
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        F_out <= (Frequency_base + V_control) * Multiplier;
    end
endmodule

The PLL should lock to the frequency of the incoming signal and adjust its output clock accordingly. Design a fan speed controller that adjusts the speed of a fan based on a 3-bit input representing temperature levels. The fan has three speed settings: low, medium, and high. The fan speed should change on the rising edge of a clock signal. The temperature levels are defined as follows: 0-2 (low), 3-5 (medium), and 6-7 (high). When the temperature input is outside the defined range (e.g., higher than 7), the fan should stop.

);

            3'b011, 3'b100, 3'b101: fan_speed <= 2'b01; // Medium speed
            3'b110, 3'b111: fan_speed <= 2'b10; // High speed

endmodule

description: Design a Verilog module for a thermal sensor calibration system that takes a raw temperature reading and calibrates it based on a given offset value. The calibrated temperature should be outputted after a specific number of clock cycles, allowing for a delay in processing. The system should have an enable signal to start the calibration process. Design a 32-bit deserializer that takes an 8-bit input and outputs a 32-bit value. The input data is valid when an enable signal is high. The deserializer should shift in the 8-bit value every clock cycle when the enable signal is active. The output should be valid after 4 clock cycles.

Design a temperature-based shutdown controller that activates when the temperature exceeds a specified threshold. The system should monitor the temperature continuously and trigger an "overheat" signal if the temperature remains above the threshold for a certain number of clock cycles. The shutdown signal should only be asserted once the overheat condition has been confirmed for the specified duration.
code:
module temp_shutdown_controller(
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [7:0] temperature, // Input temperature signal
    input [7:0] threshold,   // Overheat threshold
    output reg overheat,     // Overheat signal
    output reg shutdown       // Shutdown signal
);
    parameter COUNT_LIMIT = 4; // Number of cycles to confirm overheat
    reg [1:0] count; // Counter for overheat confirmation
    reg overheat_detected;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            count <= 0;
            overheat <= 0;
            shutdown <= 0;
            overheat_detected <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (temperature > threshold) begin
                if (overheat_detected) begin
                    if (count < COUNT_LIMIT - 1) begin
                        count <= count + 1;
                    end else begin
                        shutdown <= 1; // Trigger shutdown after COUNT_LIMIT
                    end
                end else begin
                    overheat_detected <= 1;
                    count <= 1; // Start counting
                end
            end else begin
                overheat_detected <= 0;
                count <= 0;
                shutdown <= 0; // Reset shutdown if temperature is normal
            end
            overheat <= overheat_detected; // Update overheat status
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple sliding window protocol for reliable data transmission. The sliding window size is fixed at 4 frames. Implement a sender module that can send frames and a receiver module that can acknowledge received frames. The sender should wait for an acknowledgment before sending the next frame when the window is full. The module should also handle wrap-around in the window.

Design a 4-bit LIFO stack in Verilog. The stack should support push and pop operations. It should have inputs for pushing data, a pop operation, and an output for the current top value of the stack. The stack should also have a full signal that indicates if the stack is full and an empty signal that indicates if the stack is empty.
code:
module LIFO_stack (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input push,
    input pop,
    input [3:0] data_in,
    output reg [3:0] data_out,
    output reg full,
    output reg empty
);
    reg [3:0] stack [0:15]; // 16 deep stack
    reg [3:0] top;           // points to the top of the stack

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            top <= 4'b0000; // Reset stack pointer
            empty <= 1'b1;
            full <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (push && !full) begin
                stack[top] <= data_in; // Push data
                top <= top + 1;
                empty <= 1'b0;
                if (top + 1 == 16) 
                    full <= 1'b1; // Stack is full
            end
            if (pop && !empty) begin
                top <= top - 1;
                data_out <= stack[top]; // Pop data
                if (top == 1)
                    empty <= 1'b1; // Stack is empty
                full <= 1'b0;
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

If the control signal is high, the GPIO pin should be set to high; if low, it should be cleared.

The DMA controller should receive requests from two channels (channel A and channel B) and grant access to one of the channels based on a round-robin scheduling algorithm. The controller should have enable signals for both channels, and it should generate a grant signal for the currently active channel.

Design a pulse generator that produces a single pulse of specified width and period based on input control signals. The pulse generator should have the following inputs: 
1. clk (clock signal)
2. start (start signal to initiate the pulse)
3. width (pulse width in clock cycles)
4. period (total period in clock cycles)
The output should be a single pulse signal (pulse) that is high for the specified pulse width and then low, after which it resets and waits for the next start signal.
code:
module pulse_generator(
    input clk,
    input start,
    input [3:0] width,
    input [3:0] period,
    output reg pulse
);
    reg [3:0] count;
    reg [1:0] state; // 0: idle, 1: generating pulse, 2: waiting for next pulse

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        case(state)
            0: begin
                pulse <= 0;
                count <= 0;
                if (start) begin
                    state <= 1; // Start generating pulse
                end
            end
            1: begin
                pulse <= 1;
                count <= count + 1;
                if (count >= width) begin
                    state <= 2; // Finished generating pulse, wait for period
                    count <= 0;
                end
            end
            2: begin
                pulse <= 0;
                count <= count + 1;
                if (count >= period) begin
                    state <= 0; // Go back to idle state
                end
            end
        endcase
    end
endmodule

The first stage of the pipeline will perform an increment operation on the input, while the second stage will double the result from the first stage. Design a Verilog module that simulates a simple Flash memory cell. The module should have a single data input (D), a write enable control signal (WE), and an output (Q) that reflects the stored value. When WE is high, the value of D should be stored in Q; when WE is low, Q should maintain its current value. Additionally, implement a reset input (RST) that, when asserted, sets Q to 0 regardless of WE. The output Q should be 1 bit wide.

);

    end else begin

    end

It should include an input for data, a write enable signal to enqueue data, a read enable signal to dequeue data, and output data and status signals.

Design an Adaptive LMS filter in Verilog that updates its weights based on the input signal and desired output signal. The filter should take in an input signal, a desired signal, and an adaptive step size as inputs. It should output the filtered signal and the updated weights.
code:
module adaptive_lms_filter(  
    input clk,  
    input rst,  
    input [15:0] x,      // Input signal  
    input [15:0] d,      // Desired signal  
    input [15:0] mu,     // Step size  
    output reg [15:0] y, // Output signal  
    output reg [15:0] w  // Updated weights  
);  
    reg [15:0] error;  
    reg [15:0] product;  
  
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin  
        if (rst) begin  
            y <= 16'b0;  
            w <= 16'b0;  
        end else begin  
            y <= w * x; // Output signal calculation  
            error <= d - y; // Error calculation  
            product <= mu * error * x; // Update product  
            w <= w + product; // Update weights  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

description:
Design a linear voltage regulator with the following specifications:
- The input voltage (Vin) can range from 0 to 5V.
- The output voltage (Vout) should be regulated to 3.3V if Vin is greater than or equal to 3.3V.
- If Vin is less than 3.3V, Vout should equal Vin.
- The output voltage should be represented as a 4-bit binary number ranging from 0V to 5V in increments of 0.3125V (i.e., 0V = 0000, 0.3125V = 0001, ..., 5V = 1111).
code:
module voltage_regulator (
    input [3:0] Vin, // 4-bit input representing Vin in 0.3125V increments
    output reg [3:0] Vout // 4-bit output representing Vout in 0.3125V increments
);

        if (Vin >= 4'd11) // 3.3V = 11 in 0.3125V increments
            Vout = 4'd11; // Output 3.3V
        else
            Vout = Vin; // Output Vin
    end
endmodule

description: Design a deadbeat controller for a discrete-time linear system in Verilog. The controller should take a current state and reference input and compute the next state using a deadbeat control strategy.

Implement state transitions for sending and receiving frames and acknowledgments.

Design a temperature-based shutdown system using Verilog. The system should monitor the temperature and enable a shutdown signal if the temperature exceeds a certain threshold. The system should have a clock input, a reset input, a temperature input, and an output shutdown signal. The shutdown signal should remain high until the temperature drops below a safe level and the reset is applied.
code:
module temperature_shutdown(
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [7:0] temperature,
    output reg shutdown
);
    parameter THRESHOLD = 8'd100; // Temperature threshold for shutdown
    parameter SAFE_TEMP = 8'd80;   // Safe temperature to reset shutdown

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            shutdown <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (temperature > THRESHOLD) begin
                shutdown <= 1; // Activate shutdown
            end else if (temperature < SAFE_TEMP) begin
                shutdown <= 0; // Deactivate shutdown
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

                        state <= 2'b01; // Move to service state

    input wire reset,
    input wire kick,
    output reg safe
);
    parameter TIMEOUT = 4; // 4 clock cycles timeout
    reg [2:0] counter; // 3-bit counter

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            counter <= 0;
            safe <= 1; // system is safe
        end else begin
            if (kick) begin
                counter <= 0; // reset counter on kick
                safe <= 1; // system is safe
            end else if (counter < TIMEOUT) begin
                counter <= counter + 1; // increment counter
                safe <= 1; // system is still safe
            end else begin
                safe <= 0; // system is reset
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

module stop_and_wait_arq(

    input rst,
    input send_data,
    input ack,
    input nack,
    output reg data_out,
    output reg retransmit
);

        if (rst) begin
            state <= 0;
            data_out <= 0;
            retransmit <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                0: begin // idle
                    if (send_data) begin
                        data_out <= 1; // send data
                        state <= 1;
                    end
                end
                1: begin // sending
                    state <= 2; // move to waiting for ACK

                2: begin // waiting

                        data_out <= 0; // acknowledge received

                        state <= 3; // move to retransmitting
                    end

            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

);

- An output signal `ack` (1 bit) that acknowledges the request.
- An output signal `data_out` (8 bits) that carries the response data.
- A clock signal `clk` and a reset signal `rst`.

The logic should work as follows:
- On reset, `ack` should be low and `data_out` should be 0.
- When `request` is high, the module should acknowledge the request (`ack` goes high) and output the `data_in` on `data_out` after one clock cycle.
- The `ack` signal should return low after one clock cycle of being high.

module pcie_request_handler (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire request,
    input wire [7:0] data_in,
    output reg ack,
    output reg [7:0] data_out
);
    reg state;  // 0 = idle, 1 = processing

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            ack <= 0;
            data_out <= 0;
            state <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                0: begin // Idle state
                    ack <= 0;
                    if (request) begin
                        data_out <= data_in;
                        ack <= 1;
                        state <= 1; // Move to processing state
                    end
                end
                1: begin // Processing state
                    if (ack) begin
                        ack <= 0; // Acknowledge the request
                        state <= 0; // Go back to idle
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

- 10: Weakly Taken
- 11: Strongly Taken

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        // Update the counter based on branch outcome
        case (counter)
            2'b00: begin
                if (branch_outcome) counter <= 2'b01; // Move to Weakly Not Taken
                predicted_outcome <= 0; // Predict Not Taken
            end
            2'b01: begin
                if (branch_outcome) counter <= 2'b10; // Move to Weakly Taken
                predicted_outcome <= 0; // Predict Not Taken
            end
            2'b10: begin
                if (branch_outcome) counter <= 2'b11; // Move to Strongly Taken
                else counter <= 2'b01; // Move to Weakly Not Taken
                predicted_outcome <= 1; // Predict Taken
            end
            2'b11: begin
                if (~branch_outcome) counter <= 2'b10; // Move to Weakly Taken

        endcase

module pll (

    input wire reset,          // Reset signal
    output reg clk_out         // Output clock

            clk_div <= 0;

            clk_div <= ~clk_div;   // Toggle divided clock
            div_count <= 0;        // Reset counter

        end

    always @(posedge clk_ref or posedge reset) begin

            clk_out <= 0;

    end
endmodule
